How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** – complete with real‑world snippets – that shows exactly how to build & fire a *REST* request against **Cisco Nexus Dashboard v6.3.1** to pull “Device Connector Versions” data. > ⚠️ > All URLs below assume your instance runs on `https://{dshost}`. Replace `{dshost}`, `` and `` with values specific to your environment. --- ## 1️⃣ Authentication ‑ Get an Access Token ### 1.1 Client‑Credentials Flow `device_connector_versions` requires the scope `nx_dashboard.read`. (See the official docs → *Authentication → Scopes*) ```bash POST https://{dshost}/oauth/token Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded grant_type=client_credentials&scope=nx_dashboard.read ``` #### Curl Example ```bash TOKEN=$(curl -skS --request POST \ --header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \ --data-urlencode "grant_type=client_credentials" \ --data-urlencode "scope=nx_dashboard.read" \ --basic-auth ":" \ "https://${dshost}/oauth/token" | jq -r .access_token) echo $TOKEN ``` #### Python (`requests`) Example ```python import requests token_endpoint = f"https://{dshost}/oauth/token" payload = {"grant_type": "client_credentials", "scope": "nx_dashboard.read"} response = requests.post( token_endpoint, data=payload, auth=("YOUR_CLIENT_ID", "YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET") ) access_token = response.json()["access_token"] ``` Once you own the bearer token, all subsequent calls just prepend it into the `Authorization` header. --- ## 2️⃣ Build the Request | Element | Value | |------------------|-------| | Method | `GET` | | Endpoint | `/api/v1/deviceConnectorVersions` | | Host | `https://{dshost}` | | Headers | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | > 👉 If you’re not sure what the exact URI is, open the **Developer Console** inside Nexus Dashboard: > > 1. Log in → **Settings** → **API Explorer** > 2. Browse the catalog until you see *“Get Device Connector Versions”*. > 3. Copy the full path shown next to the *Request URL* field. ### Query Parameters (Optional) | Param | Description | Typical Values | |------|-------------|---------------| | `limit` | Max number of items per page | e.g., `50`, `100` | | `offset` | Pagination cursor | integer starting at `0` | | `sortBy` | Field to order by | `"version"` , `"releaseDate"` | | `filter[status]` | Filter by status | `"active"`, `"deprecated"` | Example URL with paging + sorting: ``` https://{dshost}/api/v1/deviceConnectorVersions?limit=25&offset=0&sortBy=releaseDate ``` --- ## 3️⃣ Send the Call ### 3a) Using `curl` ```bash curl -kSs \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ "https://${dshost}/api/v1/deviceConnectorVersions?limit=20" # Pretty‑print with jq curl ... | jq . ``` ### 3b) Using Python (`requests`) ```python import json, sys, requests base_url = f"https://{dshost}" endpoint = "/api/v1/deviceConnectorVersions" query_params = { "limit": 20, # add more keys here if needed } headers = { "Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}", "Accept": "application/json" } res = requests.get(base_url+endpoint, headers=headers, params=query_params, verify=False) # set verify=True in prod! if res.ok: print(json.dumps(res.json(), indent=2)) else: print(f"[ERROR] {res.status_code}: {res.text}", file=sys.stderr) ``` > 🔒 **Tip:** Never ship `verify=False`; enable SSL verification in production. --- ## 4️⃣ Sample Response Structure A typical successful reply looks like this (truncated): ```json { "totalCount": 42, "pageSize": 20, "currentPage": 1, "items": [ { "id": "dc-v10.5.1", "name": "Device Connector V10.5.1", "description": "Stable release supporting NXOS 9.x", "releaseDate": "2023-07-12T00:00:00Z", "supportedDevices":[ "NX-9000 Series", "NX-7000 Series" ], "status": "ACTIVE" }, ... ] } ``` Fields you’ll often care about: | Key | Meaning | |-----|---------| | `id` | Unique identifier used when installing/updating connectors | | `name` | Human readable label | | `releaseDate` | When the connector was published | | `supportedDevices` | List of platform families | | `status` | `ACTIVE`, `DEPRECATED`, … | Pagination metadata (`totalCount`, `pageSize`, `currentPage`) lets you loop through all records. --- ## 5️⃣ Handling Errors | Status Code | Reason | What to Do | |------------|--------|-----------| | `401 Unauthorized` | Invalid/missing token | Refresh token or re‑authenticate | | `403 Forbidden` | Insufficient permissions | Verify scope (`nx_dashboard.read`) | | `404 Not Found` | Wrong endpoint | Double‑check the URL | | `429 Too Many Requests` | Rate limiting | Back off, retry after `Retry-After` header | | `500 Internal Server Error` | Backend issue | Contact support or try again later | Always inspect the body of non‑200 responses – the API returns helpful messages. --- ## 6️⃣ Automating Paging Here’s a quick helper that pulls *all* pages automatically: ```python def fetch_all_vers(): url = f"{base_url}{endpoint}" params = {"limit": 50, "offset": 0} while True: r = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, verify=False) r.raise_for_status() data = r.json() yield from data["items"] if len(data["items"]) < params["limit"]: break params["offset"] += params["limit"] for item in fetch_all_vers(): print(item["name"]) ``` --- ## 7️⃣ Quick Test Inside Nexus Dashboard If you’d rather hit the API directly from the web console: 1. Go to **Admin ➜ Developer Tools ➜ API Explorer**. 2. Search for *“Device Connector Versions”*. 3. Click **Execute** – the tool will auto‑populate the Authorization header based on your session cookie. 4. Inspect the raw request/response right away. This is handy for debugging before scripting. --- ## 🎉 Wrap‑Up Checklist ✅ [ ] Grab a valid OAuth2 token (`client_credentials`). ✅ [ ] Construct the correct endpoint (`/api/v1/deviceConnectorVersions`). ✅ [ ] Add necessary headers (`Authorization`, `Accept`). ✅ [ ] Optionally supply query params (`limit`, `offset`, `sortBy`). ✅ [ ] Handle pagination if you expect > N entries. ✅ [ ] Check for errors and act accordingly. Happy querying! 🚀
